correctness.rationale: For each integer pair 0≤ell<h, exact dx/2 moments make opposite-parity fourth-power ratio Q(s)=A(1-s)^2+B s^2+2Cs(1-s). The signed factorization C-B=-2(2h+1)P(h)/[(4h+1)(2h+2ell+1)], P(h)=2h²-(10ell+4)h-(2ell+1), and P(5ell+2)=-(2ell+1), P(5ell+3)=8ell+5 prove the exact integer transition. Completing the square or factoring Q-B establishes globally sharp values and all equality cases. The same-parity first derivative at pure x^h is -8h(h-ell)/[(3h+ell+1)(h+ell+1)]≠0; the lower endpoint is handled analogously, including ell=0. Direct substitution gives the asymptotic limit. Exact-rational independent binomial integration tests 2936 opposite-parity pairs and same-parity local obstructions, without relying on finite tests as universal proof.

value.rationale: The exact sharp L2→L4 embedding norm of a natural two-degree Müntz subspace tests whether adding a distant lower-degree monomial actually improves the extremal fourth moment. The all-pair classification establishes a non-arbitrary universal lacunarity threshold: mixed extremizers through degree 5ell+1, rigid high-degree extremizers from 5ell+3, and no pure extremizer for same-parity powers. The exact positive gain (C-B)^2/(2C-A-B), coefficient ratio and limiting degree-ratio-five transition characterize a structural approximation-space phenomenon not supplied by general density/Remez or Markov bounds. It is a complete sharp two-generator invariant, not offered as a multi-generator theorem.
